A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of a strong thermocline is the main prerequisite for the development of calcareous cyst populations.
the presence of a thermocline is a necessary, but not a sufficient condition for calcareous dinocyst accumulation in the equatorial regions of the Atlantic Ocean.

The main takeaway from our work is that

calcareous dinocyst assemblages are more sensitive to changes in the vertical structure of the water column than to changes in bioproductive conditions, which is in contrast to the situation in the North Atlantic.

the distribution patterns of the calcareous dinocyst record in the equatorial region cannot simply be explained by the distribution of the calcarean algae, which are known to be more abundant in oligotrophic environments.
the distribution of calcareous cysts in sediment records can be used to reconstruct past stratification of the surface water column, which is not necessarily linked to oligotrophy.
